1933: the Japanese-Manchukuo offensive on Rehe. 'On February 23, 1933, the offensive was launched'; 'On February 25 Chaoyang and Kailu were taken'; the battle was fought 'from February 21 to March 1, 1933'.

1933: Chengde falls. 'On March 4 Japanese cavalry and the 1st Special Tank Company with Type 89 tanks took Chengde'; the Chinese 'fell back in disarray to the Great Wall'; the Tanggu Truce later set up a demilitarised zone between the Great Wall and Beijing (no date on the page).
4 March 1933: Rehe is annexed to Manchukuo. Infobox: 'Rehe Province got annexed on the 4 March 1933'; the Manchukuo page repeats 'Rehe annexed: 4 March 1933'.

4 March 1933: Rehe joins the client state. Infobox 'Rehe annexed: 4 March 1933' (Manchukuo page), the same page's puppet-state status applying to the enlarged state. Recorded from the vassal's side (manchukuo is the vassal, empire-of-japan the suzerain); the Japan dossier carries the mirror event with counterpart manchukuo (empire-of-japan /ledger/43). [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added at the reviewer's request (check 3, vassal mirror); page re-read the same day.]

1 March 1934: Puyi is enthroned and Manchukuo becomes an empire. 'Manchukuo was proclaimed a monarchy on 1 March 1934, with Puyi assuming the throne with the era name of Kangde'; Manchoutikuo or Empire of Manchou became the official English names. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

wars.name: Japanese invasion of Manchuria
wars.outcome: Japan overran Manchuria: 'At the war's end in February 1932, the Japanese established the puppet state of Manchukuo'; 'On February 27, 1932, Ding offered to cease hostilities, ending official Chinese resistance in Manchuria'; 'The occupation lasted until mid-August 1945'.
wars.note: Page opened 2026-10-25 for the repair; it dates the war's end (February 1932) but not the proclamation (18 February or 1 March 1932 are on the Manchukuo page) and says nothing of the Xing'an lands or Rehe. The infobox start 18 September 1931 is on the Manchukuo page; the fighting itself is in the fengtian-clique dossier.

wars.name: Battle of Rehe
wars.outcome: Japanese-Manchukuo victory: Rehe was annexed to Manchukuo on 4 March 1933 and the Tanggu Truce created a demilitarised zone between the Great Wall and Beijing.
wars.note: Fought 21 February - 1 March 1933 on the page's infobox, with Chengde taken on 4 March.

wars.name: Battles of Khalkhin Gol

zones.text: the disputed Manchukuo-Mongolia border at the Khalkhin Gol river and Nomonhan (no gazetteer name; the coordinate is the researcher's placement of the river, not a page figure)

wars.outcome: Status quo ante bellum on the infobox: 'enforcement of border claims in accordance with the Soviet and Mongolian interpretation'; no land changed hands between the states' own holdings. 'The Soviet Union and Japan agreed to a cease-fire on 15 September; it took effect the following day'; 'In 1941, the two countries signed agreements respecting the borders of Mongolia and Manchukuo.'
wars.note: 11 May - 16 September 1939 (infobox). 'The Japanese maintained that the border between Manchukuo and Mongolia was the Khalkhin Gol'; the Mongolians and Soviets held that it ran 16 km east of the river, just east of Nomonhan. Soviet commander Zhukov; Japanese 23rd Division under Komatsubara. [ea-08-x repair 2026-10-25: added at the reviewer's request; the certainty note already named the battles.]

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Manchuria

zones.text: Dolon Nur and Kalgan in Mengjiang

wars.outcome: Soviet victory: the page's infobox lists 'the collapse of the Japanese puppet states'; 'Most of Manchuria and Inner Mongolia are returned to the Nationalist government of China by a 1945 bilateral agreement'; the Red Army withdrew 'by 3 May 1946'.

certainty.note: The Great Wall frontier is fought over until Rehe falls (March 1933); the Xing'an lands have no boundary on any page opened.
Provincial and railway lines are administrative records; the frontier with Mongolia was disputed in 1939 (Khalkhin Gol, summer 1939 on the Manchukuo page) and stays soft.

notes:
Written by ea-08-x on 2026-10-24 from five pages. No Cliopatria row exists for Manchukuo; the Empire of Japan row (jk-01) carries Manchuria as Japanese land, so the renderer should draw this dossier's shapes over it (the Japan dossier already records Manchukuo as a vassal_start 1932). Family 'china' is a suggestion; the colour agent may prefer 'japan' for the Japanese client states.

Not settled: (1) the Xing'an lands (Hulunbuir, Hinggan, Jirem): the administrative-divisions page names a Xing'an Province in 1932 but gives no date or boundary, so the gain is at confidence 1 and the keyframes use radii round Ulanhot and Tongliao; (2) the 1934 and 1939/1941 provincial reorganisations are not dated on the pages and move no outer border; (3) the date and terms of the Tanggu Truce are not on the Battle of Rehe page (it gives no date); (4) when the South Manchuria Railway Zone passed to Manchukuo is not given (Kwantung page only says Japan transferred it); (5) the end: infobox 20 August 1945, text 'September', Puyi's abdication 15 or 17 August; (6) the Japanese invasion of September 1931 to February 1932 is dated only by the infobox line; a gap-filler should open 'Japanese invasion of Manchuria' (the fengtian-clique dossier uses it if opened). Gazetteer: 'Jehol/Rehe', 'Chahar' and 'Suiyuan' are missing (Chengde 160 km used for Rehe, as the Republic of China and Empire of Japan dossiers do). The Manchukuo page's wikidata id is not known to the researcher (null).
